Accountable obligation owner.value: Filing-analyst function performed by the Regulatory Filing Specialist; escalation to Regulatory Affairs Manager for state-specific bottlenecks and to Regulatory Counsel for statutory disputes

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 45 CFR 156.410 (QHP certification standards) and 156.420 (denial of certification), re-read against the current CMS Letter to Issuers and each state's SERFF Filing Rules ahead of every plan-year review cycle

In-scope processes.value: Annual individual-market QHP rate and form filing review cycle — from initial SERFF/CMS submission through every objection letter, interrogatory and corrective-action request issued by the state DOI or CMS Plan Management, for all on- and off-Exchange individual health products

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Objection Letters tab (state DOI review) and CMS Plan Management (PM) Community / HIOS interrogatory correspondence; both tracked in the Internal Regulatory System objection log

Compliance procedure documented.value: Objection & Interrogatory Response Procedure — daily queue monitoring, triage matrix by objection type, routing rules, response drafting standard, sign-off gate, and submission checklist

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; reviewed each plan year ahead of the rate/form filing window and on any CMS Letter to Issuers update

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per objection — state-specific response windows (commonly 10-21 calendar days per the state's SERFF Filing Rules) computed from the objection letter date; CMS PM Community interrogatories carry their own HIOS-notified due date, both counting toward the September 30 QHP certification finalization deadline

Deadline reminders configured.value: Objection log milestone alerts at 50% of the response window elapsed and 2 days before due, plus a standing countdown to the September 30 certification finalization date for any objection still open

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Objection log, each objection letter, the response package and submission confirmation retained 7 years from the plan year's last effective date in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any objection response filed after the state/CMS deadline, or any objection left unanswered, is logged as an exception with root cause and remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off any late or escalated objection response and any corrective action plan filed with CMS or the state DOI

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All objection letters and CMS interrogatories issued against the individual health product's SERFF/CMS filings in the plan-year review cycle, drawn from the objection log across every filing state

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for missed response deadlines; any objection answered after the state/CMS due date, or a certification denied under 45 CFR 156.420 for non-response, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per objection; test runs annually at the close of the plan-year review cycle (post-September 30) over 100% of that cycle's objections

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: must not have drafted or routed any sampled objection response

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual objection-response test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Objection log export plus each objection letter, response package and SERFF/HIOS submission timestamp, presentable to CMS or the state DOI within 5 business days of request

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager owns the CMS/state DOI inquiry response; Regulatory Counsel clears any response that concedes a late or incomplete answer before it is sent

checklist.step: Monitor the SERFF Objection Letters queue and CMS Plan Management correspondence daily
actions: Log in to SERFF and open Filing Access; filter Status = 'Objection Issued' or 'Deficient' for each state where the individual health filing is pending.
Open the CMS Plan Management (PM) Community/HIOS module and check the Issuer inbox for interrogatories or corrective-action requests tied to the QHP certification review.
For each new objection or interrogatory, note the issuing regulator, filing SERFF Tracking Number or HIOS submission ID, and the date issued.
Notify the Product Filing Specialist and Product / Filing Actuary of any objection touching their filed elements the same business day.
checklist.done: every objection or interrogatory issued since the prior check is captured with issuer, tracking number and issue date.

checklist.step: Triage and classify each objection by subject
actions: Classify the objection type: actuarial/rate (URRT, rate exhibits), form/EHB benchmark, network adequacy, CSR plan variation, or other.
Determine the state's response window from the SERFF Filing Rules page for that state and TOI.
Compute due date = objection issue date + response window, and flag prior-approval-state objections as highest priority.
Assign a preliminary owner based on the classification.
checklist.done: each objection has a subject classification, a computed due date and an assigned owner.

checklist.step: Log the objection into the Objection Log
actions: Create a log row with change/filing id, state, SERFF Tracking Number, objection text summary, classification, due date, owner and status = 'Open'.
Attach the objection letter PDF to the row.
Link the row to the filing's determination folder for traceability back to the original filing rows.
checklist.done: a log row exists with a citation summary, due date, owner and the attached objection letter.

checklist.step: Route actuarial/rate objections to Product / Filing Actuary for a rebuttal analysis
actions: Read the URRT or rate exhibit line item the objection cites.
Re-derive the trend, morbidity or benefit-relativity assumption in question and compare it to the objection's stated concern.
Prepare a rebuttal memo or a revised rate exhibit with an updated actuarial certification page.
Return the memo or exhibit to the Regulatory Filing Specialist with the turnaround time stated.
checklist.done: a rebuttal memo or a revised, certified rate exhibit is ready for inclusion in the response.

checklist.step: Route form/EHB benchmark objections to Product Filing Specialist for a redline
actions: Compare the cited form or benefit provision against the state's EHB benchmark plan crosswalk.
Produce a compliant redline of the form with a bumped edition date.
Attach the benchmark comparison supporting the redline.
Note whether the change requires a Statement of Variability update and prepare it if so.
checklist.done: a compliant redline exists with a benchmark comparison attached and any needed Statement of Variability update prepared.

checklist.step: Route statutory/legal objections to Regulatory Counsel
actions: Read the cited statute or CFR section (e.g., 45 CFR 156.410, 156.420, 147.126, 156.130) as issued in the objection.
Assess whether the objection is valid or contestable under the current regulatory text.
Draft the legal-position paragraph to be included in the response letter.
Flag any objection that could plausibly lead to certification denial under 156.420 and notify the Regulatory Affairs Manager.
checklist.done: a legal position is drafted for the response and any denial risk is flagged.

checklist.step: Assemble the consolidated response package
actions: Combine the actuarial rebuttal, form redlines, legal position and any CSR/EHB support into a single response letter following the state's or CMS's required objection-response format.
Attach every supporting exhibit referenced in the response letter.
Verify each objection point is answered point-by-point, in the order the objection letter raised them.
checklist.done: the response package answers every objection point in order, with each supporting exhibit attached.

checklist.step: QA review the response package for completeness
actions: Check that each objection line item has a corresponding response paragraph.
Confirm every citation quoted in the response matches the current regulatory text.
Confirm all attachments open, are watermark-free and carry the correct edition date.
Flag any unaddressed objection item back to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for completion.
checklist.done: no objection line item is left unanswered and every citation checks out against current text.

checklist.step: Obtain sign-off before submission
actions: Review the full response package end to end.
Confirm the risk position taken on any contestable or denial-risk objection.
Sign off or return the package for rework with named gaps.
Record the sign-off name and date on the objection log row.
checklist.done: sign-off is recorded with a date on the log row before the response is submitted.

checklist.step: Submit the response in SERFF/HIOS within the computed deadline
actions: Log in to SERFF Filing Access, open the pending filing and use the 'Respond to Objection Letter' function to attach the response package and every exhibit.
For CMS interrogatories, upload the response through the PM Community issuer portal instead.
Submit before end of business on the computed due date.
Capture the confirmation screen and submission timestamp into the filing folder.
checklist.done: the response is submitted in the correct system before the due date, with a captured confirmation timestamp.

checklist.step: Update the Objection Log with submission confirmation
actions: Paste the SERFF submission confirmation number or HIOS confirmation timestamp onto the log row.
Set the row status to 'Responded — pending disposition'.
Recalculate any downstream milestone, including the September 30 certification date, if the response shifted it.
checklist.done: the log row shows the submission confirmation, updated status and any recalculated milestone.

checklist.step: Monitor for a second-round objection or a disposition
actions: Check SERFF Filing Access and PM Community daily for a new objection letter or a disposition (Approved/Certified, Deficient, Denied).
If a second objection arrives, restart triage at the classification step against a fresh due date.
If the disposition is Approved/Certified, route the filing to closure.
checklist.done: the filing reaches a disposition, or a new objection cycle is captured and triaged.

checklist.step: Escalate any objection approaching or past its deadline
actions: Run a daily due-date report from the Objection Log.
For any objection within 2 business days of due date with no draft ready, escalate to the Regulatory Affairs Manager and the Insurance Product Manager the same day.
For any objection already past due, open an exception and notify the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: no objection reaches its due date without an escalation record if the draft is not ready.

checklist.step: Support any denial-risk objection with a decision on withdrawal, revision or contest
actions: Where Regulatory Counsel flags certification-denial risk under 45 CFR 156.420, review the business impact with the Product / Filing Actuary and Regulatory Counsel.
Decide to revise the filed element, withdraw the affected product or state, or contest the objection in writing.
Record the decision and its owner on the objection log row — leaving the objection unanswered is never one of the options.
checklist.done: every denial-risk objection carries a written, owned decision on the log row.

checklist.step: Close the log entry and file the objection record for retention
actions: On disposition, set the log row to 'Closed — Approved' (or Denied/Withdrawn) with the disposition date.
Move the objection letter, response package and submission confirmation into the compliance evidence repository under state, product and plan year.
Apply the 7-year retention label so the record survives the plan year.
checklist.done: the log row is closed with a disposition date and the record is filed under the 7-year retention label.

testing.step: Build the population of objections/interrogatories issued in the plan-year cycle
actions: Export the SERFF Filing Access objection history for every individual-health state filing in the cycle.
Export the CMS PM Community interrogatory list for the same cycle.
Combine and reconcile the counts to the Objection Log; resolve any gap before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the Objection Log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to a logged response and disposition
actions: Match each population row to an Objection Log row on the SERFF/HIOS tracking number.
Check that a response submission timestamp and a final disposition exist for the row.
List any unmatched or dispositionless row as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a logged, dispositioned response or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of objections carrying a denial-risk flag or arising in a prior-approval state.
Take 20 additional rows at random, seeded and reproducible, for a minimum of 30 sampled rows.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every denial-risk and prior-approval-state row.

testing.step: Recompute the response deadline for each sampled objection
actions: Re-read the issuing state's SERFF Filing Rules response window (or the HIOS-notified due date) as of the objection date.
Recompute due date = objection issue date + response window.
Compare the recomputed due date to the log's recorded due date and to the actual submission timestamp.
testing.done: the recomputed due date matches the log for every sampled row, and any late submission is flagged.

testing.step: Re-perform the response content check against the objection text
actions: Read the original objection letter line by line for each sampled row.
Read the submitted response package for the same row.
Confirm every objection point has a substantive, citation-backed answer.
Flag boilerplate or unanswered points as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled response substantively answers every objection line, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Trace the submission to the system of record
actions: Open SERFF Filing Access (or PM Community) for each sampled filing.
Locate the response submission and its timestamp.
Confirm the attached exhibits match what is stored in the compliance evidence repository.
Capture the SERFF/PM Community screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled submission is confirmed in the regulator system with a matching exhibit set.

testing.step: Verify sign-off evidence
actions: Confirm the Regulatory Affairs Manager sign-off date on the log pre-dates the submission timestamp for each sampled row.
Confirm any denial-risk decision carries the Insurance Product Manager's named decision and date.
testing.done: sign-off and denial-risk decisions are dated and pre-date submission for every sampled row.

testing.step: Check escalation discipline on any late or near-miss row
actions: For any sampled row submitted within 1 day of due date or after, confirm an escalation record exists at the Compliance Officer/Regulatory Affairs Manager level.
Where no escalation exists for a late response, log a control-design exception.
testing.done: every late or near-miss row has a corresponding escalation record, or a logged exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the state, filing, objection and the type of miss.
Assign a root cause (queue not checked, wrong response window, actuary turnaround, sign-off delay) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missed-deadline threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor, as independent reviewer, sign the workpaper.
Report results and any denial-risk or late-response exceptions to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Compliance Ops archival function performed by the Compliance Analyst; escalation to Compliance Manager for retention-schedule exceptions and gaps found in the annual completeness sweep

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — recordkeeping obligation implied by CMS's oversight and audit authority under 45 CFR 156.410/156.420 (QHP certification and denial standards), re-read against the current CMS Letter to Issuers recordkeeping expectations and each state's SERFF record-retention statute

In-scope processes.value: Continuous archival of every CMS/state approval letter, disposition notice, and the corresponding final filed form, rate exhibit and URRT version for each individual health product certified for the plan year

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Filing Access disposition history and attachments; approvals mirrored into the compliance evidence repository and Microsoft 365 / SharePoint for indexed long-term storage

Compliance procedure documented.value: Filing Archive & Retention Procedure — capture trigger (disposition = Approved/Certified), document capture checklist, indexing taxonomy, retention labeling, access control and disposal review

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; reviewed annually alongside the enterprise records-retention schedule and on any change to CMS/state retention requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous — each approval/disposition must be archived within 5 business days of receipt in SERFF/PM Community; no external filing deadline, but the September 30 certification finalization date drives the plan year's archive-completeness checkpoint

Deadline reminders configured.value: Archive-queue alert 5 business days after a disposition is logged with no matching archive record; annual completeness-sweep reminder set for October 15, after the September 30 certification finalization date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Approval/disposition letter, the final filed form/rate/URRT version as approved, and the SERFF/PM Community confirmation retained 7 years from the plan year's last effective date (10 years where a state statute sets a longer period) in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any disposition found without a matching archived approval letter or filed version, or any retrieved record that does not match the approved edition, is logged as an exception with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off completion of any archive-gap remediation and any retention-schedule exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All CMS/state disposition events (Approved/Certified/Closed) recorded in SERFF/PM Community for the individual health line in the period, drawn from the Filing Determination Log and Objection Log disposition fields

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for missing archive records; any disposition with no archived approval letter, or an archived version that does not match the approved edition, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; test runs annually after the September 30 certification finalization date over 100% of that plan year's dispositions

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: must not have performed any sampled archive capture

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual filing-archive completeness test workpaper (population extract, sample, retrieval notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Archive index export plus each retrieved approval letter and filed version, presentable to CMS or the state DOI within 5 business days of an audit or market conduct exam request

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Manager owns the CMS/state DOI records-request response; Records Manager retrieves and certifies the record set before it is sent

checklist.step: Detect every new disposition event that triggers an archive obligation
actions: Check SERFF Filing Access weekly for filings that moved to Disposition = Approved, Certified, Filed or Closed-Approved for individual health products.
Check CMS PM Community for QHP certification notices and Corrective Action Plan closures.
Cross-reference the disposition list against the Filing Determination Log and Objection Log to catch every filing awaiting archive.
Note the disposition date for each item identified.
checklist.done: every new disposition since the last check is identified with its disposition date.

checklist.step: Capture the official approval/disposition letter
actions: In SERFF Filing Access, open the filing and download the Disposition Letter/Notice of Filing attachment.
In PM Community, download the QHP Certification Notice or CMS approval correspondence.
Verify the letter carries the SERFF Tracking Number or HIOS submission ID, the state or CMS letterhead, and the disposition date.
Save the file as <state>-<product>-<plan year>-disposition-letter.pdf.
checklist.done: the disposition letter is downloaded, verified against its tracking number, and saved under the naming convention.

checklist.step: Capture the final filed/approved version of each artifact
actions: Retrieve the exact form, rate exhibit, URRT and rating manual page version bearing the edition date that was approved, not a later working draft.
Compare the retrieved edition date to the one referenced in the disposition letter.
Flag and re-pull the artifact if the edition dates do not match.
checklist.done: the retrieved artifact version's edition date matches the disposition letter exactly.

checklist.step: Index the archive record
actions: Create an archive index entry with state, product, TOI/Sub-TOI, SERFF Tracking Number/HIOS ID, disposition date and plan year.
Add a pointer to where the disposition letter and filed version are stored.
Tag the entry against the corresponding Filing Determination Log row.
checklist.done: an index entry exists, linked to its source determination log row, with all key fields populated.

checklist.step: Store the record set in the compliance evidence repository and SharePoint
actions: Upload the disposition letter and filed version set into the compliance evidence repository under Product ▸ State ▸ Plan Year.
Mirror the index metadata into the SharePoint filing archive library for day-to-day retrieval.
Set folder permissions to Compliance and Regulatory Filing roles only.
checklist.done: the files exist in both the evidence repository and SharePoint with matching metadata and restricted access.

checklist.step: Apply the retention label
actions: Apply the 7-year-from-last-effective-date retention label (or the longer state-specific period where one applies) to the record set.
Confirm the label is machine-readable in the repository's retention management feature.
Record the calculated disposal-eligible date on the index entry.
checklist.done: every archived record carries a retention label and a calculated disposal-eligible date.

checklist.step: Cross-check the archive against the Objection Log for fully-resolved filings
actions: For every filing closed in the Objection Log, confirm the final response package and the ultimate disposition letter are both archived, not just the original submission.
Where an objection cycle produced a revised edition, confirm the archived filed version is the final, post-objection approved edition.
checklist.done: the archived filed version matches the final, post-objection approved edition for every closed objection.

checklist.step: Reconcile weekly against the SERFF/PM Community disposition list
actions: Pull the week's disposition list from SERFF Filing Access and PM Community.
Match each row to an archive index entry.
List any disposition without a matching archive entry as an open item with an owner.
checklist.done: every disposition in the week's list is matched to an archive entry, or carried as an open item with an owner.

checklist.step: Escalate any archive gap open beyond 5 business days
actions: Review the open-item list from the weekly reconciliation.
For any item open past 5 business days, escalate to the Compliance Analyst's manager and the Regulatory Filing Specialist who owns the underlying filing.
Request the missing artifact directly from SERFF/PM Community if the original owner cannot supply it.
checklist.done: no archive gap remains open past 5 business days without an escalation record.

checklist.step: Run the annual completeness sweep after the certification finalization date
actions: After September 30, pull the full plan-year disposition list from SERFF Filing Access and PM Community.
Compare the list row-for-row against the archive index.
Produce a completeness report with any gaps highlighted.
checklist.done: a completeness report exists covering 100% of the plan year's dispositions with gaps identified.

checklist.step: Remediate any gap found in the completeness sweep
actions: For each gap, re-retrieve the disposition letter and filed version from SERFF/PM Community, or request a certified copy from the state DOI/CMS if the portal copy is unavailable.
Complete the index entry with the retrieved documents.
Note the remediation date on the completeness report.
checklist.done: every gap from the sweep is closed with the record archived and the remediation date logged.

checklist.step: Review access permissions on the filing archive quarterly
actions: Run a permissions report on the compliance evidence repository and the SharePoint filing archive library.
Confirm access is limited to Compliance, Regulatory Filing and Internal Audit roles.
Remove any stale or excess access and log the review date.
checklist.done: the access report is reviewed, stale access is removed, and the review date is logged.

checklist.step: Test retrieval on a rotating sample
actions: Each quarter, pick 5 archived filings at random.
Retrieve the disposition letter and filed version from the repository without consulting the original filing team.
Confirm both documents open, are legible, and match the index metadata.
checklist.done: all sampled retrievals succeed and match the index metadata every quarter.

checklist.step: Apply legal hold where litigation or a regulatory inquiry is active
actions: Where an examination, complaint or litigation touches a filing, place a legal hold flag on the record in the repository, overriding the standard disposal-eligible date.
Notify the Records Manager of the hold and its scope.
checklist.done: every filing under active inquiry or litigation carries a logged legal hold overriding disposal.

checklist.step: Review and execute disposal only after the retention period and clear of holds
actions: Run the disposal-eligible report from the repository.
Confirm no legal hold flag is present on any record on the report.
Obtain Compliance Manager sign-off before permanent disposal.
Log the disposal date and the sign-off.
checklist.done: no record is disposed without a hold-clear check and a signed Compliance Manager approval, logged with the disposal date.

testing.step: Build the population of dispositions requiring an archived record
actions: Extract every SERFF/PM Community disposition (Approved/Certified/Closed) for the individual health line across the plan year.
Reconcile the extract count to the Filing Determination Log and Objection Log disposition fields.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the underlying logs and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the archive index
actions: Match each population row to an archive index entry by SERFF Tracking Number/HIOS ID.
List any disposition with no matching index entry as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population row is matched to an archive index entry or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of dispositions tied to a prior objection cycle (revised editions).
Take 15 additional rows at random, seeded and reproducible, for a minimum of 25 sampled rows.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every revised-edition row.

testing.step: Retrieve and inspect the archived record set for each sampled row
actions: Open the compliance evidence repository entry for the sampled row.
Confirm both the disposition letter and the filed version are present, legible and unredacted.
Confirm the filed version's edition date exactly matches the disposition letter.
testing.done: each sampled row's archive contains a matching, legible letter and filed version.

testing.step: Trace the archived version back to the SERFF/PM Community system of record
actions: Open SERFF Filing Access (or PM Community) for the sampled filing.
Download the disposition letter and filed attachment directly from the regulator system.
Compare the downloaded copy against the archived copy field-by-field.
Capture the SERFF/PM Community screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: the archived copy matches the regulator system's copy for every sampled row, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify the retention label and disposal-eligible date
actions: For each sampled row, confirm the retention label reflects 7 years (or the longer applicable state period) from the correct last-effective-date anchor.
Recompute the disposal-eligible date and compare it to the system-calculated value.
testing.done: retention labels and disposal-eligible dates are correctly calculated for every sampled row.

testing.step: Confirm legal holds are honored
actions: Cross-check the sample against the active litigation/examination list.
Confirm any matching filing carries a logged legal hold overriding its disposal-eligible date.
Flag any hold that was missed as an exception.
testing.done: every filing under active inquiry in the sample carries a logged hold, or the miss is flagged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify access controls on the archive
actions: Pull the current permissions list for the compliance evidence repository and SharePoint filing archive library.
Confirm access is restricted to Compliance, Regulatory Filing and Internal Audit roles.
Flag any unexpected grantee as an exception.
testing.done: the access list matches the approved role set, or unexpected access is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the filing, state and gap type (missing letter, edition mismatch, missing hold, access issue).
Assign a root cause and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-missing-record threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor, as independent reviewer, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
